claims.claim: The office door was closed with the latch engaged and there were no signs of forced entry at the office door or back door.
claims.quote: The office door was closed and the latch engaged. There were no signs of forced entry at the office door or the back door.

claims.claim: A league scoresheet dated November 4 was on the office desk.
claims.quote: On the desk was a league scoresheet dated November 4.

claims.claim: The lane 12 ball return cover was open, the rest of the lanes were dark, and the office keypad showed a green ready light.
claims.quote: The cover of the lane 12 ball return stood open. The rest of the lanes were dark. The keypad panel beside the office door showed a green ready light.

claims.claim: Carla Ibanez died of homicide by blunt force injury to the head between 11:30 p.m. on November 4 and 1:30 a.m. on November 5, 2017.
claims.quote: Cause of death: blunt force injury to the head. Manner: homicide. Based on body temperature and rigor, the time of death is estimated between 11:30 p.m. on Saturday, November 4, 2017 and 1:30 a.m. on Sunday, November 5, 2017.

claims.claim: There were no defensive wounds, a single injury pattern was noted, and the instrument was not recovered at the scene.
claims.quote: There were no defensive wounds. A single injury pattern is noted; the instrument was not recovered at the scene.

claims.claim: He has worked as the night mechanic at Starlite Lanes for six years fixing pinsetters and ball returns.
claims.quote: I am the night mechanic at Starlite Lanes. I have worked there six years. I fix the pinsetters and the ball returns.

claims.claim: He came in at 6:00 PM on Saturday to work on lane 7, finished the belt job, left at 11:00 PM, and never returned.
claims.quote: Saturday I came in at six to work on lane 7. I finished the belt job and I left at eleven and never went back.

claims.claim: Carla Ibanez was fine and in the office doing the books when he left at 11:00 PM.
claims.quote: Carla was in the office doing the books when I left. She was fine.

claims.claim: He drove home and passed the building around 12:30 AM on his way to get cigarettes, observing the building, lanes, and office dark with nobody there.
claims.quote: I drove home. I passed the building again around twelve thirty on my way to get cigarettes and the building was dark, lanes off, office dark. Nobody was there.

claims.claim: Carla Ibanez cut his weekday hours in October.
claims.quote: She cut my weekday hours in October, sure, but that is business.

claims.claim: Handwritten log entries state he replaced the lane 7 belt at 9:40 PM, signed out at 11:00 PM, and checked lane 12 at 1:03 AM under the date Sat 11/4.
claims.quote: Sat 11/4 - 9:40 PM - lane 7 belt replaced. Sat 11/4 - 11:00 PM - out. Sat 11/4 - 1:03 AM - checked lane 12, all good.

claims.claim: He captains the Saturday league at Starlite Lanes.
claims.quote: I captain the Saturday league at Starlite.

claims.claim: He returned to Starlite Lanes on Saturday night for his bowling ball, letting himself in at 11:20 PM using his own code.
claims.quote: I left my ball in the locker room Saturday night, so I went back for it. I let myself in at 11:20, on my own code.

claims.claim: Carla Ibanez was alive in the office working on scoresheets when he entered at 11:20 PM, and they talked for a minute about the league banquet.
claims.quote: Carla was in the office. We talked for a minute about the league banquet. She was alive and fine and working on the scoresheets.

claims.claim: He took his ball and left without seeing anyone else in the building.
claims.quote: I took my ball and left. I did not see anybody else in the building.

claims.claim: He worked the counter at Starlite until Carla Ibanez fired him on October 12 for allegedly shorting the register, which he denies.
claims.quote: I worked the counter at Starlite until Carla fired me on October 12. She said I was shorting the register. I was not.

claims.claim: In his 2017 statement, he claimed he was home all Saturday night and did not go near Starlite Lanes.
claims.quote: Saturday night I was home all night. I did not go near the lanes. I have no reason to go back there and I did not.

claims.claim: In his 2019 statement, he stated he drove to the Starlite lot around 11:10 PM for his last paycheck, knocked on the back hall office door with no answer, saw the office window was dark, and left before 11:40 PM without going inside.
claims.quote: I got to the lot around eleven ten. I knocked on the office door off the back hall. Nobody answered. The office window was dark from where I stood. I left before eleven forty. I never went inside.

claims.claim: He stated he gave a false account in 2017 because of how it would look for a fired employee to be at the door that night.
claims.quote: I lied in 2017 because I knew how it would look, a fired man at the door that night.

claims.claim: In a 12:41 AM text to Andre Ibanez, the sender stated Tommy was there again and was told to log it.
claims.quote: Outgoing text, 12:41 AM, November 5, to Andre Ibanez: "tommy is here again. told him if he is going to be here he logs it this time"

claims.claim: In her 2025 statement, she stated she remembered the machines running and pins resetting on lane 12 while she mopped the back hall.
claims.quote: While I mopped the back hall I remember the machines running on lane 12, the pins resetting.

claims.claim: Josefina Luna was home by 12:30 AM that night.
claims.quote: Josefina was home by 12:30 that night. I remember because I waited up; we were going to watch the fight replay and it started without her.

claims.claim: The faulty rear service door latch mechanism from 2016 was replaced on January 9, 2017, and latched all twenty times when tested.
claims.quote: Item 14, rear service door: the latch mechanism reported faulty in 2016 was replaced on January 9, 2017. The door was tested twenty times and latched every time.

claims.claim: She told Det. Alvarez she took a photo from the parking lot at 12:55 AM on November 5 showing the Starlite Lanes office window lit with the blinds partly open.
claims.quote: League member Diane Pruitt told me she took a photograph from the parking lot at 12:55 AM on November 5, showing the office window of Starlite Lanes lit, with the blinds partly open.

claims.claim: Diane Pruitt showed him the 12:55 AM photograph on her phone on November 12, 2017, but the original was never collected before she replaced the phone.
claims.quote: She showed me the photograph on her phone during our conversation on November 12. The original photograph was never collected. Ms. Pruitt has since replaced the phone.

claims.claim: A handwritten margin note on the October 1, 2017 roster restricted Reyes to weekends only starting October 1.
claims.quote: Margin note, in the owner's hand: "From Oct 1, Reyes to weekends only - C.I."

On Sunday, November 5, 2017, at 0605 hours, Officer P. Tate responded to Starlite Lanes, 88 Meridian Avenue, after the morning opener found owner Carla Ibanez, 47, deceased on the office floor behind the counter (doc01). She was pronounced dead at 0622 hours (doc01), and the medical examiner ruled the death a homicide caused by blunt force injury to the head from an unrecovered instrument, estimating the time of death between 11:30 PM on November 4 and 1:30 AM on November 5 (doc02). Marcus Bell entered the office on keypad code 4410 at 11:20 PM (doc05; lot gate 11:18 PM - 11:29 PM, doc09) and reported speaking with Ibanez while she was alive and working on scoresheets (doc06). Inside the 11:30 PM - 1:30 AM death window, digital logs and witness accounts record Derek Hahn's pickup in the lot until 11:38 PM (doc09), back hall and office corridor motion between 11:36 PM and 1:19 AM (doc11), office keypad entries using codes 3308 (11:41 PM), 2214 (12:52 AM), and 7712 (1:03 AM) (doc05), an outgoing text from Ibanez's phone at 12:41 AM stating "tommy is here again" (doc10), a 12:55 AM witness photo of the lit office window (doc17), and a 1:03 AM mechanic's log entry for lane 12 by Tomas Reyes (doc04). At the scene, the lane 12 ball return cover stood open and a November 4 league scoresheet lay on the office desk (doc01).

THE STRONGEST CONTRADICTION
Tomas Reyes's alibi that he left Starlite Lanes at 11:00 PM and only passed a dark, empty building around 12:30 AM directly fights the victim's phone records, the mechanic's sign-out log, and the parking lot gate reader:
- Statement (doc03): "I finished the belt job and I left at eleven and never went back." / "I passed the building again around twelve thirty on my way to get cigarettes and the building was dark, lanes off, office dark. Nobody was there."
- Record (doc10): "Outgoing text, 12:41 AM, November 5, to Andre Ibanez: \"tommy is here again. told him if he is going to be here he logs it this time\""
- Corroborating Records (doc04, doc09): The mechanic's log contains the handwritten entry "Sat 11/4 - 1:03 AM - checked lane 12, all good." below "Sat 11/4 - 11:00 PM - out." (doc04), and the lot gate reader shows "Plate ending 2093, blue sedan, registered to T. Reyes: entered 6:01 PM, no exit read that night." (doc09).
